rationale: The core method is right for the design: DESeq2 negative-binomial Wald test on raw integer counts for an unpaired 3v3 single-batch comparison, with an explicit and quantitative treatment of low power (dispersion diagnostics, MDE/power estimation, leave-one-out stability) that correctly avoids lowering alpha. QC is concrete and precedes testing (library size, count distribution, PCA/clustering colored by condition), and the sample-count reconciliation gate is a good touch, though no explicit outlier-handling policy is stated. Filtering relies solely on DESeq2's post-hoc independent filtering with an explicit ban on pre-filtering, so the minimal justified low-count filter of the reference is only partly satisfied; normalization is handled correctly by keeping raw counts out of any pre-normalization but size factors are never named. The design formula and reference level are never written out — only 'condition as the design factor, treated vs control' — which is thin for the model criterion. Enrichment is the weakest part: it is not clearly warranted by the question, and the ORA that is included specifies no background universe, no collection version, and no gene-set size window, only a minimum overlap; the report is otherwise complete except for tool versions.
